entries.title: Job 30:1
segments: Great prosperity may speedily be followed by great afflictions.  None, therefore, should be unduly lifted up by the one, or cast down by the other.  Both are under the control of God; and in both, the great object of all should be to known him.

entries.title: Job 30:2
segments: Old age was perished; they were prematurely old and feeble on account of their poverty.

entries.title: Job 30:3
segments: Fleeing into the wilderness; they were vagabonds, shunning the society of their fellow-men.

entries.title: Job 30:4
segments:
Mallows; a plant like spinach, the leaves of which are used by the poor, both cooked and raw, as a relish for their bread. 
 
  Juniper-roots; the Hebrew word denotes a species of broom, the roots of which are very bitter, and are used for making charcoal. Compare

. 
 
  For their meat; that is, for their living or sustenance.  The roots were probably not eaten, but either used for cooking their food, or sold to obtain food.

entries.title: Job 30:5
segments: They were driven forth; on account of their crimes.

entries.title: Job 30:7
segments: Brayed; uttered their cries.

entries.title: Job 30:8
segments: Viler than the earth; or driven out from the earth; that is, from the habitable earth into the desert.

entries.title: Job 30:9
segments: To be the song of the drunkard and the jest of the vilest of mankind has often been the lot of the virtuous; especially of those who have been active in bringing punishment upon the vicious.

entries.title: Job 30:11
segments:
He; God. 
 
  Loosed my cord; taken away my former authority, by which they were overawed and restrained. 
 
  Let loose the bridle; cast off all restraint in afflicting me.

entries.title: Job 30:12
segments:
Raise up against me; this is a figure taken from military operations.  They cast up their mounds against me as a besieging army against a fortress. 
 
  The ways of their destruction; ways, that is, embankments, that have for their object to destroy me.

entries.title: Job 30:13
segments: They have no helper; they need no one either to incite them, or help them complete their work of destruction.

entries.title: Job 30:17
segments:
My bones are pierced; expressive of the keenest and most aggressive pain. 
 
Bodily diseases are often more distressing, and the pains which they occasion are harder to bear, than any can realize, except those who endure them; and when such are neglected and reviled by those who ought to pity and relieve them, the evil is greatly increased.

entries.title: Job 30:18
segments: My garment changed; defiled and made stiff from my running sores. But some understand the word garment to refer to his skin, which is disfigured and made stiff by his sores.

entries.title: Job 30:20
segments:
Thee; God. 
 
  Dost not hear; dost not remove my distress. 
 
When good men in distress cry unto God, though he hears and will eventually answer, and do exceeding abundantly above all that they ask, yet he may not, and often does not, at once relieve them; but calls them to let patience have its perfect work, that thus they may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.

entries.title: Job 30:23
segments: The nearness and certainty of death should lead all to be habitually prepared for it; and though deeds of mercy for Christ's sake will not secure uninterrupted prosperity in this world, not even the giving of a cup of cold water to his disciples will fail of an abundnat reward in the life to come.

entries.title: Job 30:24
segments: Howbeit--in his destruction; the meaning of this verse is uncertain.  Some propose to render it thus: Surely there can be no prayer [prayer can avail nothing] when he [God] stretcheth out his hand: in his calamity [when God sends calamity upon a man] shall there then be a cry? [can a cry to God avail any thing?]

entries.title: Job 30:25
segments: Did not I weep; at the calamities of others, when he was in prosperity.

entries.title: Job 30:26
segments: I looked for good; in connection with his charitable deeds.

entries.title: Job 30:27
segments: Prevented; went before, came upon me.

entries.title: Job 30:29
segments:
Dragons; the original word means beasts of the desert, like jackals, that are noted for their mournful cry. 
 
  Owls; or ostriches, also well known as raising a loud cry, which much resembles the roar of the lion.
